data.source_title: The management of suspected scaphoid fractures in the UK: a national cross-sectional study
data.locator: Methods, Outcomes; Results, Primary outcome: MRI availability directly from ED
data.source_setting: 87 UK centers treating acute wrist trauma; clinician surveys across ED, minor injury and orthopaedic services
data.source_n: 87 participating centers; 11 reported MRI directly available from ED
data.quantity: Centers reporting direct-from-ED MRI imaging capability for suspected scaphoid fracture
data.source_evidence_basis: In a clinician-survey cross-sectional study, 11 of 87 centers (13%) reported MRI directly available from the ED for suspected scaphoid fracture. This measures service/pathway capability reported by centers, not whether a scanner or slot was free at a given time or whether a patient received imaging promptly.
data.limitations: UK suspected-scaphoid pathway, clinician self-report and possible sampling bias; no timestamped scanner utilization, queue, staffing or case-level access measurement. Not an estimate of MRI availability in New Brunswick or elsewhere in the US.
data.inferred_scenario_use: Represent modality/service capability separately from scheduled operating hours, staffing, queue state, occupied slot and patient-specific eligibility. Do not convert capability percentage into a free-slot probability.
